transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I just don’t feel like doing anything anymore—not cooking, not music, not even playing dominoes with my friends. My daughter got worried because I've been so quiet since we moved from our house, so she arranged for us to talk.
How long ago was your move, and have you also been feeling down or sad most of the day since then?

We moved into this apartment about a year and five months ago. I wouldn't say I feel sad or like crying, but I just feel completely flat, like there is no spark left inside me and nothing means anything anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since these feelings started?

My sleep has changed a lot, especially during those times when I feel completely wired and only sleep two or three hours a night, sitting by the window making plans. As for my appetite, I haven't really noticed any major changes or I'm not too sure about that.
During those times when you feel wired and sleep very little, how long do those periods usually last, and do you also feel unusually energetic or have racing thoughts?

Those wired spells usually last for weeks at a time, and they've been happening off and on for most of this past year. During those times, I feel like a motor that won't turn off, cleaning the apartment at midnight because I have so much energy. My thoughts also race so fast that I jump from one topic to another in a matter of seconds, and I can't slow them down to finish a single idea.
During those times when you feel so energetic and wired, has it ever caused any problems in your daily life or relationships, or have you ever needed to be hospitalized because of it?

Yes, it causes a lot of strain because I get very irritable and snap at my wife and daughter, or stay up all night trying to start repairs on things that aren't even mine. It got so disorganized that my daughter had to take over managing my bills and medicine, but I've never had to go to the hospital because of it.
During these times when your mood shifts so dramatically, were you taking any new medications, or using alcohol or other substances?

No, I don't drink alcohol or use any other substances. As for my medicine, I only take my usual daily pills, but my daughter manages them all for me now so I'm not really sure if there have been any changes.
During those times when you felt extremely energetic or wired, did you ever hear or see things that others couldn't, or hold very strong beliefs that others found highly unusual?

Yes, even on those high-energy days, I still hear a man's voice calling my name and telling me I'm failing my mission. I also can't shake the feeling that the neighbors are watching me and testing me to see if I'm still fit to live on my own.
Do you ever hear that voice or feel like your neighbors are watching you during the times when your energy is normal or when you feel flat, rather than wired?

Yes, even during those quiet, flat times when my energy is normal, I still hear that man's voice talking to me and feel like the neighbors are watching. There have been several stretches over this past year, lasting for weeks at a time, where I didn't feel high or low at all but the voice and the testing didn't stop. It is very tiring and I just can't seem to shake it.

latest_inference.note: The candidates remain F25 (Schizoaffective disorder) and F31 (Bipolar affective disorder). The patient describes manic-like episodes (periods of high energy, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, irritability) and depressive-like periods (flatness, loss of interest). Crucially, the patient reports that auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions persist for weeks during periods of normal mood. This key detail strongly supports F25 over F31, as psychotic symptoms in bipolar disorder typically occur only during mood episodes. We now have sufficient clinical history to make a confident diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with concurrent symptoms of a mood disorder (both manic and depressive phases) and schizophrenia-spectrum psychotic symptoms. Crucially, the patient experiences auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions during periods of normal mood lasting for weeks at a time, fulfilling the DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder (F25) rather than Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (F31), which requires psychotic symptoms to occur exclusively during mood episodes.
